explanation: Temperate deciduous forests are located south of the taiga in eastern North America, eastern Asia, and throughout much of Europe. This biome is characterized by a moderate climate, relatively high rainfall, and four distinct seasons featuring a long growing season. The tallest trees grow close together to form a canopy. Ground-level life is highly abundant. Notably, amphibians and reptiles are common in these forests, unlike in the taiga, because the winters are not cold enough to exclude them.

questions.q: Why are amphibians and reptiles found in temperate deciduous forests but generally absent from the taiga?
opts: Deciduous forests have acidic peat bogs that protect them.
Winters in temperate deciduous forests are not as cold as in the taiga.
The trees in deciduous forests do not form a canopy, letting in more light.
Amphibians and reptiles feed exclusively on deciduous tree bark.
